analysis.title: "Panic Without A Washout": Goldman's Coppersmith Says Hedge Funds Have Puked... Everyone Else Is Still Long
key_insights: GS Vol Panic Index closed Friday at 9.8 out of 10 with SPX below 7k. Across 42 episodes at 9 or above, the S&P averaged +4.4% over three months and was higher 78% of the time.
Hiking regimes weaken the panic-buy signal. In five episodes with panic above 9 during a hiking Fed, three-month returns averaged just +0.4%, versus +4.6% when on hold and +5.4% when cutting.

Hedge funds have capitulated. Prime brokerage data shows a third straight week of global equity selling, short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1, and the biggest weekly US single-stock shorting since June 2022.

Fundamental L/S net leverage is 42.3% (1st percentile of past year). Beta-adjusted net leverage is 48.2%, a five-year low, down from an 84.6% spring peak. The gap between reported and beta-adjusted leverage has largely disappeared.
Momentum exposure went from a record +70% in June to negative, the lowest since late 2022. GS VIP basket lags the S&P by 14pp over six months.

Other cohorts remain long. GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at the 75th percentile (+0.7), nearly $170B has flowed into US equity MFs and ETFs since Q4 began, and asset manager futures length is at the 82nd percentile. Past big buying opportunities came at -2.5 to -3.0.

Best historical outcomes (+6.7% over three months, higher 94% of the time) came with a non-hiking Fed and negative sentiment. Today's combination of hiking Fed and positive sentiment averaged about +1.6% from three observations.

Q4 2018 analog: October 2018 panic was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months. High-beta cyclicals (GSXUHBCY) are up 12% YTD at 15x fwd PE, a 40% premium to the 2018 trough multiple, and fell 23% in 4Q18. Broad AI basket is negative YTD.

GS frames an AI earnings fork of roughly 5,800 on the S&P if valuations normalize on trend earnings versus 8,100 if confidence in consensus earnings returns. From ~6,910 that is about 16% downside versus 17% upside. Forward multiple has fallen from 23x to 16x.
Sustainable recovery needs AI earnings confidence, a more dovish Fed, or further positioning reduction. Only the last has shown up, and mainly within hedge funds.
CTAs are short $11.3B S&P futures, $4B Russell and $3.6B Nasdaq but long $11.4B FTSE and $11.2B DAX. US selling is largely done and they would be buyers on a bounce.
Technicals are fragile. Dealer gamma is negative into the holiday week and S&P futures top-of-book depth is the lowest since April 2025, so moves in either direction can be violent.

Goldman's trade: underwrite vol by selling puts at levels where one would add length, especially in tech where vol repricing is most extreme. VXN at 45 is the highest since COVID and VXSMH at 78 is an all-time high. Goldman sees a near tactical entry.
The writer expects a short sharp bounce but argues the broader washout and Fed relief are not in place, so the December 2018 script may have more to run.

sector_views.rationale: Still up 12% YTD at a 40% premium to the 2018 trough multiple, and vulnerable if growth uncertainty replaces inflation anxiety.
Vol repricing is extreme, so selling puts is preferred over chasing stocks, with no call on the bottom.

earnings_insights: The AI earnings debate is the key swing factor. GS Research sees S&P outcomes of roughly 5,800 (valuation normalization on trend earnings) to 8,100 (consensus earnings regained and multiples recover).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Close to the 15x level where the 2022 bear market bottomed.
A hiking Fed weakens the historical panic-buy signal, and a stock slide may be what stops it.
Roughly symmetric risk of 16% downside and 17% upside from ~6,910.

trade_ideas.description: Sell puts on tech and semis at levels where the investor would be comfortable adding length (strikes not specified)
trade_ideas.rationale: Vol is panicked while positioning has not fully washed out, so this gets paid to take equity risk with lower entry levels if the unwind continues.
trade_ideas.risk: Downside exposure if this becomes a more sustained selloff.

risk_factors: Fed continues hiking and does not rescue markets.
Broader investor positioning remains elevated, with a risk of further selling by long-onlys, retail and asset managers.
Q4 2018 repeat with another leg lower.
Thin holiday liquidity with negative gamma and poor depth.
High-beta cyclicals could underperform sharply if growth fears take over.

vol_and_positioning: GS Vol Panic Index at 9.8 out of 10 on Friday.
VXN closed at 45, the highest since COVID. VXSMH closed at 78, its series all-time high. The front of the vol curve is sharply inverted.
Dealer gamma is negative into Thanksgiving week and S&P futures depth is at the lowest since April 2025.
Fundamental L/S net leverage is 42.3% (1st percentile of past year), beta-adjusted 48.2% (five-year low), and momentum exposure is negative.
ETF shorts rose 11% on the week. Fundamental L/S lost 1.2% Friday, and US-focused managers lost 1.6% (a 2.6 standard deviation move). Stock pickers are down 2.1% in November while quants are up 1.5%.
CTAs are short $11.3B S&P, $4B Russell and $3.6B Nasdaq futures, and would be buyers on a bounce.
cross_bank_references: JPMorgan thinks the real money hasn't sold yet.
BofA's Michael Hartnett said stocks need to give up all of 2026's gains for the Fed to stop hiking.
JPMorgan's John Schlegel said the S&P briefly bounced in late November 2018 before selling off more in December.
Brian Garrett's playbook ends at S&P 6,294.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol panic at 9.8 has historically preceded +4.4% three-month S&P returns, hedge funds are at extreme lows in leverage, CTAs would buy a bounce, and the forward multiple has fallen to 16x.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed is hiking, broader sentiment is still positive at the 75th percentile with ~$170B of inflows, and Q4 2018 saw another 6.8% decline after the October panic.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further selling by long-only, retail and asset manager cohorts, or a Fed that continues hiking, would invalidate the bounce thesis. A more dovish Fed or AI earnings confidence would confirm it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Vol panic and hedge fund capitulation support a tactical entry, but broad investor positioning has not washed out.
theme_stances.evidence: not the broad investor washout that has historically produced the strongest rebounds

theme_stances.key_argument: Underwriting overshot vol is a better tactical expression than buying delta.
theme_stances.evidence: we'd rather be underwriting some of this volatility than chasing stocks
